column2: For years the Winds have slipped through your fingers like smoke. Tonight, at last, they answer. The words you have mouthed a thousand times catch fire on your tongue, and the candle before you gutters in a wind that does not blow. You are a true spellcaster now, however humble.

After years of hard work and gruelling practice, your command of the Winds has grown. You are no longer limited to the simplest cantrips, and those who would oppose you should take heed of your new-found power.
Your spells now reach heights few mortals ever grasp. Lesser wizards fall silent when you enter a room, and only fools would dare stand in your way.
The Winds of Magic roar through you like a storm through an open door. You are now one of the mightiest spellcasters of the age, and even the thought of defying your will makes men tremble.
At last!
I can feel the power!
This power is amazing!
Behold my power, and despair!
While contemplating the mysteries of the Winds of Magic, you have an epiphany about a theorem that has long evaded your grasp. You are that much closer to becoming an even more powerful spellcaster.
A breakthrough!

You are ready to perform the ritual. The more of your dark power you pour into it, the greater the horde that will claw its way out of the earth to obey you. At least until the magic fades and it falls apart once more.
All shall fall and serve me in death!
A great host to bring fear to my enemies.
A large horde to serve my every need.
A small horde, nothing excessive.
Only a few servants for my personal needs.
As the last words of the ritual fade, a few hundred skeletons and rotting corpses drag themselves from the earth and stand before you, awaiting your command.
As the last words of the ritual fade, a few hundred skeletons and rotting corpses drag themselves from the earth. There are more of them than you called for. The dead here are restless.
The ground splits and heaves. Thousands of skeletons and shambling dead rise from forgotten graves and battlefields, ready to obey your every order.
The ground splits and heaves. Thousands of skeletons and shambling dead rise from forgotten graves and battlefields, and still more come. The land here remembers many deaths.
A great host of undead of every kind answers your call: skeletons in rusted mail, fresh corpses still in their shrouds, carrion birds that should not fly. The ritual has borne a fine harvest.
A great host of undead of every kind answers your call: skeletons in rusted mail, fresh corpses still in their shrouds, carrion birds that should not fly. They are more numerous than you dared hope.
When the ritual ends, the land around you has withered to grey dust and a great host of the dead fills the fields, silent and waiting.
When the ritual ends, the land around you has withered to grey dust and a host of the dead fills the fields so thickly you can barely see the ground they stand on.

Only the Great Necromancer himself could have outdone this. You have drunk every drop of life from the land, and an endless tide of corpses has risen to follow your will. Far away in Nagashizzar, something takes notice.
Good.
All the better.
The magic binding your horde has run its course. One by one the dead collapse where they stand, devoid once more of any semblance of life. You may raise another.
Dust to dust.
Daggers in the Night

You cast your sight along the threads of fate, and what moves in darkness is laid bare. One who plots against you and yours stands revealed, stripped of the shadows that hid [plot_reveal_magic.GetHerHim]: [plot_reveal_magic.GetTitledName].
You cast your sight along the threads of fate, searching for daggers in the dark. The threads are quiet. If anyone plots against you or yours, it is no one you can find.
I see you!
Good. For now.
Your hidden schemes are no match for the sorcerous gaze of [From.GetTitledName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] knows what you have been planning, and half your backers have melted away.
Confound [From.GetHerHis] sorcery!
You uncork one of the elixirs in your possession. Each is said to sharpen a different talent of the mind.
The Elixir of the Marshal.
The Elixir of the Diplomat.
The Elixir of the Steward.
The Elixir of the Spy.
Not now.

Warpstone is slightly warm to the touch and has no smell at all. Raw, it is poison to every living thing: those who handle it too long go mad, mutate and die, and those who eat it crave more than any other drug. Yet it holds the raw stuff of magic, and the desperate and the ambitious eat it all the same.
Swallow the dust.
Swallow the shard.
Swallow the whole cluster.
Not now.
You look over the potions in your possession. Each promises something different.
The Potion of Healing.
The Potion of Beauty.
The Potion of Speed.
The Potion of Strength.
Eaten raw, these mushrooms send mad visions crawling through the mind and strange strength through the body. The goblin shamans swear by them. The goblin shamans are also mostly dead.
Eat the Scarlet Elf Cap.
Eat the Madcap.
Your spell washes over the camp. Wounds close, fevers break and weary men stand straighter. Sickness flees the province.
Back on your feet, all of you.
You unleash your magic on the enemy around you. Men burn, scream and fall, and those left standing waver.
Let them break.
You speak the words of unbinding. Summoned daemons wail and fade, the risen dead fall still, and the taint lifts from the land.
Begone!
You reach into the Winds around you and tear them away from your enemies. Their wizards gasp, empty, and their soldiers feel the cold of it.
Now you are nothing.
Your magic seeps into the soil. Crops rot in the fields, wells turn foul, and the province grows poorer.
Let them starve.
Your spell sucks the life from the land. Grass greys, trees weep black sap, and the province will bear the taint for years to come.
Let it wither.
The gold you conjured from lead has quietly turned back into lead. Half the wealth your spell made is gone, and some merchants are asking awkward questions.
No magic lasts forever.
Your magic flows through the province like spring rain. Harvests swell, the sick recover, and the people prosper.
Let it flourish.
At your word, sickness blooms in the province. Fevers spread from house to house, and the bells toll for the dead.
Grandfather would be proud.
A sweet, languid haze settles over the province. Farmers doze in the fields and soldiers forget their posts, too content to care.
Sleep, my pretties.
A burning wind from the deep desert sweeps over the province, scouring the fields with sand and choking the roads.
Let the sands take it.
The sky darkens and a howling blizzard buries the province in ice and snow.
Let them freeze.

Your prisoner [magic_target.GetFirstName] stares at you through the bars as you begin to chant. Wyssan's Wildform will strip away what makes [magic_target.GetHerHim] a person and leave a beast in [magic_target.GetHerHis] place. That is, if [magic_target.GetSheHe] does not resist.
Let us see what you really are.
On second thought, no.
Bones crack and stretch. Fur bursts through your skin, your jaw lengthens into a snout, and your screams turn into a bellow. When it is over, the thing in the cell barely remembers its own name.
*Roar*
You shrink. Your skin turns cold and wet, your eyes bulge, and the cell around you becomes vast. You try to curse [From.GetTitledName], and only a croak comes out.
*Croak*
Your nose flattens into a snout and bristles sprout from your skin. You fall to all fours, and the curses you hurl at [From.GetTitledName] come out as squeals.
*Oink*
Word spreads through your court that [From.GetFirstName] now sits in a bucket in the dungeon, croaking. Your courtiers have gone noticeably quiet when you pass.
Word spreads through your court that [From.GetFirstName] now roots through the straw of the dungeon, squealing. Your courtiers have gone noticeably quiet when you pass.
Word spreads through your court of the monstrous thing that was once [From.GetFirstName], pacing and bellowing in the dungeon. Your courtiers have gone noticeably quiet when you pass.
Let that be a lesson.
No vassal will kneel to a toad, and your heirs have taken your lands in your stead. You are left with a pond, a few flies and a great deal of resentment.
No vassal will kneel to a pig, and your heirs have taken your lands in your stead. You are left with a sty and a great deal of resentment.
*Sad noises*
You feel the touch of [From.GetTitledName]'s magic clawing at your mind and body, and you throw it off. Your own power is more than a match for [From.GetHerHis].
Is that all?
Your spell slides off [From.GetFirstName] like rain off a roof. [From.GetSheHeCap] laughed at you, and word of it is spreading.
Humiliating.
You catch [From.GetTitledName]'s spell and hurl it back at [From.GetHerHim]. In the confusion that follows, the door of your cell swings open, and you walk out.
Farewell!
Your own spell rebounds on you. [From.GetFirstName] is free, and your face will never be the same.
Curse [From.GetHerHim]!

You slip into the mind of [magic_target.GetTitledName] like a thief into a sleeping house. A whisper here, a doubt there, and [magic_target.GetSheHe] will feel about you just as you wish, never knowing why.
[magic_target.GetSheHeCap] will love me.
[magic_target.GetSheHeCap] will hate me.
At your call a grove of trees groans awake, tears up its roots and lumbers to your side.
At your call the forest groans awake. Trees tear up their roots and stride to your side, branches creaking like war drums.
At your call the whole wood awakens. Ancient trees tear free of the earth and march beside you, and the ground shakes with every step.
March with me.
The trees you awakened grow slow and still and put down roots once more. The forest sleeps, and you may wake it again.
Rest, old ones.
You send your call out into the wilds. Something great answers it, padding out of the trees to join you.
Welcome, friend.
[From.GetFirstName], the beast who answered your call, has slipped away into the wilds again.
Farewell.
Your last horde of risen dead has not yet fallen apart
The last wood you awakened has not yet gone back to sleep
